Definition: from G5021; arranged, i.e. appointed or stated:--set.
BiblicalUsage: Luke says Herod, upon a set day, arrayed in royal apparel, sat upon his throne and made an oration to the people of Tyre and Sidon. The word is appointed, stated, fixed: the day was set in advance, and Herod dressed for it. It was the day the people cried out that his voice was a god's, and an angel struck him down.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Luke names the day as set on purpose: Herod planned his glory, but God had set the day too, and it ended very differently.
